records.source: וַיֹּ֥סֶף אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
records.gloss: And added Elihu and said:
pieces: Then Elihu continued:

decisions.choice: added and said: went on speaking
decisions.reason: The verb means "added": Elihu adds to what he has already said. This is the fourth of his speeches (32:6; 34:1; 35:1), the only one introduced this way, and it runs to the end of chapter 37. After it the LORD answers Job from the storm (38:1). The introduction stays prose.

decisions.choice: continued; went on speaking
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plain sense of "added" (m1), following the book's pattern for speech introductions.

records.heading: Elihu speaks for God once more

records.source: כַּתַּר־לִ֣י זְ֭עֵיר וַאֲחַוֶּ֑ךָּ כִּ֤י ע֖וֹד לֶאֱל֣וֹהַּ מִלִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Wait for me a little, and I will show you, for still for God [are] words.
pieces: Be patient with me a little longer, and I will show you \q that there is more to be said on God's behalf.

L.2: Bear with me a little, and I will show you, \q for there are still words on behalf of God.

R.2: Be patient with me a little longer, and I will explain. \q I still have more to say for God.

decisions.choice: wait for me: be patient with me
decisions.reason: The verb is rare in Hebrew; the same word is common in Aramaic for waiting. Elihu asks Job to bear with him a little longer, though he has already spoken at length (32:6-35:16).

decisions.choice: show you: declare to you, explain
decisions.reason: The verb means to make known or declare. Elihu used it when he first spoke (32:6, 10, 17: "I will declare my opinion").

decisions.choice: words for God: words in God's defense
decisions.reason: "For God" means on God's side or in his defense. Elihu's aim is to show that God is in the right (verse 3), against what Job has said (32:2).

decisions.choice: on God's behalf
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly what "for God" means here (m3).

records.source: אֶשָּׂ֣א דֵ֭עִי לְמֵרָח֑וֹק וּ֝לְפֹעֲלִ֗י אֶֽתֵּֽן־צֶֽדֶק׃
records.gloss: I will carry my knowledge from afar, and to my Maker I will give righteousness.
pieces: I will draw my knowledge from far and wide, \q and I will show that my Maker is in the right.

L.3: I will bring my knowledge from afar, \q and to my Maker I will ascribe righteousness.

R.3: I will bring together what I know from far and wide \q and show that my Maker is in the right.

decisions.choice: from afar: from a wide range, from far and wide
decisions.reason: Elihu claims a knowledge that reaches beyond the present argument. In 36:26-37:24 he draws it from the wide world of rain, storm and sky.

decisions.choice: give righteousness to: declare to be in the right
decisions.reason: To ascribe righteousness to someone is to declare that he is in the right, as in a court case. Elihu defends God against Job, who had insisted on his own righteousness rather than God's (32:2; compare 40:8).

decisions.choice: show that my Maker is in the right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the legal sense of the idiom (m2).

records.source: כִּֽי־אָ֭מְנָם לֹא־שֶׁ֣קֶר מִלָּ֑י תְּמִ֖ים דֵּע֣וֹת עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: For truly not falsehood [are] my words; [one] complete of knowledge [is] with you.
pieces: Truly, my words are not false; \q one whose knowledge is sound is here with you.

L.4: For truly my words are not false; \q one perfect in knowledge is with you.

R.4: I promise you, I am not lying. \q The one talking with you knows what he is talking about.

decisions.choice: complete in knowledge: said by Elihu of himself; sound, wholehearted knowledge
decisions.reason: The phrase is Elihu's claim for himself. The word for "complete" (tamim) is related to "blameless" in 1:1 and means whole or sound. In 37:16 almost the same phrase is used of God, which makes Elihu's claim sound bold; here it may mean only that he speaks sincerely and from sound knowledge.

decisions.choice: for truly: an emphatic assurance
decisions.reason: Elihu stresses that he is speaking honestly, not twisting the truth as he thinks Job's comforters or Job have done.

decisions.choice: one whose knowledge is sound
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the likely sense of the phrase in Elihu's mouth (m1); Literal keeps "perfect in knowledge".

decisions.choice: The one talking with you knows what he is talking about
alternatives: one perfect in knowledge is with you
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Elihu is speaking of himself.

records.source: הֶן־אֵ֣ל כַּ֭בִּיר וְלֹ֣א יִמְאָ֑ס כַּ֝בִּ֗יר כֹּ֣חַֽ לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: Look, God [is] mighty and not he rejects; mighty [in] strength of heart.
pieces: God is mighty, and yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} despises no one; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is mighty in strength of understanding.

L.5: Look, God is mighty, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not despise [anyone]; \q [he is] mighty in strength of understanding.

R.5: God is mighty, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not look down on anyone. \q His understanding is strong and great.

decisions.choice: does not reject: despises no one
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the context supplies "anyone". Job had complained that God despised the work of his hands (10:3, the same verb). Elihu answers that God's might never makes him scorn anyone.

decisions.choice: strength of heart: strength of mind and understanding
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and understanding. God is mighty not only in force but in wisdom (12:13).

decisions.choice: [anyone]; [he is]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs that the Hebrew leaves unsaid (m1).

records.source: לֹא־יְחַיֶּ֥ה רָשָׁ֑ע וּמִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיִּ֣ים יִתֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: Not he keeps alive [the] wicked, and justice of afflicted [ones] he gives.
pieces: He does not let the wicked live on, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives the afflicted their rights.

L.6: He does not keep the wicked alive, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives justice to the afflicted.

R.6: He does not let evil people go on living, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives justice to people who suffer.

decisions.choice: the afflicted: the poor and oppressed who suffer
decisions.reason: The word ('ani) means those who are poor, weak or oppressed. Elihu uses it and its noun for affliction again in verses 8 and 15.

decisions.choice: justice of the afflicted: the justice due to them, their rights
decisions.reason: The justice that belongs to the afflicted is what they are owed. Elihu answers Job's complaint that the wicked live on and prosper (21:7) while the poor suffer (24:2-12).

decisions.choice: gives the afflicted their rights
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the sense of the phrase (m2).

records.source: לֹֽא־יִגְרַ֥ע מִצַּדִּ֗יק עֵ֫ינָ֥יו וְאֶת־מְלָכִ֥ים לַכִּסֵּ֑א וַיֹּשִׁיבֵ֥ם לָ֝נֶ֗צַח וַיִּגְבָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: Not he withdraws from [the] righteous his eyes, and with kings on the throne he seats them forever, and they are exalted.
pieces: He does not take {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes off the righteous; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} seats them with kings on the throne, \q and they are raised up forever.

L.7: He does not withdraw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes from the righteous, \q and with kings on the throne \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} seats them forever, and they are exalted.

R.7: He keeps watching over people who do what is right. \q He seats them on thrones beside kings, \q and they are honored forever.

decisions.choice: not withdraw his eyes: keep watching over with care
decisions.reason: God's eyes on someone mean his watchful care (Psalm 34:16). Job had felt watched by God as an enemy (7:19-20; 14:3); Elihu says God's watch protects the righteous.

decisions.choice: with kings: the righteous are seated with kings
alternatives: he seats kings on the throne forever
decisions.reason: The small word before "kings" can mark the object or mean "with". Read as the object, the line would speak of God seating kings on the throne. In context it speaks of the righteous, whom God raises to sit with kings (compare 1 Samuel 2:8; Psalm 113:8).

decisions.choice: forever ... exalted: lastingly raised to honor
decisions.reason: The phrase means "for good" or "forever": their honor lasts. The last verb means to be lifted high.

decisions.choice: He keeps watching over
alternatives: He does not withdraw his eyes
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the eyes means (m1).

records.source: וְאִם־אֲסוּרִ֥ים בַּזִּקִּ֑ים יִ֝לָּכְד֗וּן בְּחַבְלֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And if [they are] bound in fetters, [and] they are caught in cords of affliction,
pieces: And if people are bound in chains, \q held fast by cords of suffering,

L.8: And if they are bound in fetters, \q caught in cords of affliction,

R.8: Suppose people are bound in chains \q and trapped by the ropes of suffering.

decisions.choice: if: begins a case that verses 9-10 complete
decisions.reason: Elihu describes what happens when the righteous (verse 7) or anyone fall into suffering. The "if" is answered in verses 9-10: God then shows them their wrongs. The sentence runs on, so Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: cords of affliction: suffering pictured as captivity
decisions.reason: Affliction is pictured as ropes or chains that hold a prisoner, as in Psalm 107:10. Elihu's main teaching is that God uses such suffering to warn and to save (33:16-30).

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, which the Hebrew leaves as "they" (m1).

records.source: וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לָהֶ֣ם פָּעֳלָ֑ם וּ֝פִשְׁעֵיהֶ֗ם כִּ֣י יִתְגַּבָּֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: and he declares to them their work, and their transgressions, that they behaved proudly.
pieces: then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows them what they have done, \q their transgressions, how they have acted with pride.

L.9: then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tells them their work \q and their transgressions, that they have acted proudly.

R.9: Then God shows them what they have done wrong. \q He shows them that they have been proud.

decisions.choice: transgressions: acts of rebellion
decisions.reason: The word (pesha') means rebellion or breaking faith, the most serious word for sin. God shows sufferers the wrongs behind their trouble.

decisions.choice: behaved proudly: made themselves great, acted arrogantly
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong or great. Eliphaz used it of the wicked who defy God (15:25).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who acts, which the Hebrew leaves to the pronoun.

records.source: וַיִּ֣גֶל אָ֭זְנָם לַמּוּסָ֑ר וַ֝יֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־יְשֻׁב֥וּן מֵאָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: And he uncovers their ear to discipline, and he says that they turn from wickedness.
pieces: He opens their ears to correction \q and commands them to turn back from evil.

L.10: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opens their ear to instruction \q and says that they must turn back from wickedness.

R.10: He makes them listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} warning \q and tells them to turn away from evil.

decisions.choice: uncover the ear: make someone hear, reveal something to them
decisions.reason: To uncover someone's ear is to tell or reveal something to them (1 Samuel 9:15). Elihu used the same picture in 33:16 and uses it again in 36:15.

decisions.choice: discipline: instruction through correction
decisions.reason: The word (musar) means teaching that corrects, often through discipline (5:17).

decisions.choice: says that they turn: commands them to turn
decisions.reason: The verb form after "says" expresses what God wants done: it is a command to turn back.

decisions.choice: commands
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the force of the saying (m3).

records.source: אִֽם־יִשְׁמְע֗וּ וְֽיַ֫עֲבֹ֥דוּ יְכַלּ֣וּ יְמֵיהֶ֣ם בַּטּ֑וֹב וּ֝שְׁנֵיהֶ֗ם בַּנְּעִימִֽים׃
records.gloss: If they hear and serve, they will complete their days in good, and their years in pleasant [things].
pieces: If they listen and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q they will spend their days in prosperity \q and their years in contentment.

L.11: If they listen and serve [him], \q they will complete their days in prosperity \q and their years in pleasures.

R.11: If they listen and serve God, \q they will live out their days enjoying good things, \q and their years will be pleasant.

decisions.choice: serve: serve God
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the one they serve is God, who has been speaking to them (verse 10).

decisions.choice: days in prosperity: the reward of those who turn back
decisions.reason: Elihu restates the teaching that God rewards those who listen and turn back, as Eliphaz did (5:17-26). Job had protested that the wicked also live out their days in prosperity (21:13, the same expression).

decisions.choice: [him]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object the Hebrew leaves unsaid (m1).

decisions.choice: serve God
decisions.reason: Readable names God (m1).

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֣א יִ֭שְׁמְעוּ בְּשֶׁ֣לַח יַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְ֝יִגְוְע֗וּ כִּבְלִי־דָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: And if not they hear, by [the] weapon they pass away, and they perish without knowledge.
pieces: But if they do not listen, they perish by the sword \q and die without understanding.

L.12: But if they do not listen, they pass away by the weapon, \q and they perish without knowledge.

R.12: But if they do not listen, they will die a violent death; \q they will die without ever learning.

decisions.choice: pass away by the weapon: die by violence
decisions.reason: The word (shelach) usually means a weapon such as a spear or javelin. Elihu used the same phrase in 33:18. Some take the word as a channel or river, here the river of death that the dead cross over.

decisions.choice: without knowledge: dying without having learned
decisions.reason: They die without the understanding that God's warning offered them (compare 4:21).

decisions.choice: die a violent death
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what passing away by the weapon means (m1).

records.source: וְֽחַנְפֵי־לֵ֭ב יָשִׂ֣ימוּ אָ֑ף לֹ֥א יְ֝שַׁוְּע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲסָרָֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] godless of heart put anger; not they cry for help when he binds them.
pieces: But those who are godless at heart hold on to their anger; \q they do not cry for help even when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} binds them.

L.13: But the godless in heart lay up anger; \q they do not cry for help when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} binds them.

R.13: But people who have turned from God in their hearts stay angry. \q Even when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts them in chains, they do not cry out for help.

decisions.choice: godless in heart: inwardly turned from God
decisions.reason: The word (chanef) describes someone who is godless or corrupt; Bildad and Eliphaz used it of those who forget God (8:13; 15:34).

decisions.choice: put anger: hold on to resentment
decisions.reason: They keep their anger instead of turning to God. The phrase may instead mean that they store up God's anger against themselves.

decisions.choice: binds them: the fetters of verse 8
decisions.reason: God's binding them refers back to the chains and cords of affliction in verse 8. The godless do not turn to him even then.

decisions.choice: hold on to their anger
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the more likely sense (m2).

records.source: תָּמֹ֣ת בַּנֹּ֣עַר נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְ֝חַיָּתָ֗ם בַּקְּדֵשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: Dies in youth their soul, and their life among the cult prostitutes.
pieces: They die in their youth, \q and their life ends among the shrine prostitutes.

L.14: Their soul dies in youth, \q and their life [ends] among the shrine prostitutes.

R.14: They die while they are still young, \q and their lives end in shame.

decisions.choice: their soul: they themselves, their life
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) here means the whole living person, not a soul apart from the body.

decisions.choice: shrine prostitutes: men who served at pagan shrines
decisions.reason: The word (qedeshim) names men attached to pagan shrines, whom the law forbids in Israel (Deuteronomy 23:18; 1 Kings 14:24). The exact practice is not described. Here it is a picture of a short life ended in disgrace.

decisions.choice: [ends]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the verb the Hebrew leaves to be carried over.

decisions.choice: in shame
decisions.reason: Readable gives the point of the picture (m2) rather than naming the shrine servants.

records.source: יְחַלֵּ֣ץ עָנִ֣י בְעָנְי֑וֹ וְיִ֖גֶל בַּלַּ֣חַץ אָזְנָֽם׃
records.gloss: He rescues [the] afflicted by his affliction, and he uncovers by oppression their ear.
pieces: He rescues the afflicted through their suffering \q and opens their ears through distress.

L.15: He rescues the afflicted by his affliction \q and opens their ear by oppression.

R.15: God uses suffering to rescue those who suffer; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} uses hard times to make them listen.

decisions.choice: by his affliction: suffering is the means of rescue
decisions.reason: The preposition means "by" or "through": affliction itself is how God rescues the afflicted. This is the heart of Elihu's teaching (33:19-30). The same preposition can mean "in": God rescues them while they suffer.

decisions.choice: the afflicted by affliction: a play on words
decisions.reason: The words for "afflicted" and "affliction" come from the same root: the one who suffers is saved by suffering.

decisions.choice: opens their ear: makes them hear (as verse 10)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, to uncover the ear is to make someone hear.

decisions.choice: their suffering
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the plural "their", since "the afflicted" stands for many people; the Hebrew has "his".

decisions.choice: God uses suffering to rescue
alternatives: He rescues the afflicted by affliction
decisions.reason: Readable puts the means first and names God, to make the point clear (m1).

records.source: וְאַ֤ף הֲסִיתְךָ֨׀מִפִּי־צָ֗ר רַ֭חַב לֹא־מוּצָ֣ק תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וְנַ֥חַת שֻׁ֝לְחָנְךָ֗ מָ֣לֵא דָֽשֶׁן׃
records.gloss: And also he allured you from [the] mouth of distress, [into] a broad place, not constraint beneath it, and [what was] set [on] your table full [of] fatness.
pieces: He was also drawing you out of the jaws of distress \q into a wide place with nothing to hem you in, \q to a table loaded with the richest food.

L.16: And indeed {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drew you out of the mouth of distress \q into a broad place where there was no constraint, \q and what was set on your table was full of fatness.

R.16: God also wanted to lead you out of your trouble \q into a wide-open place where you would be free, \q to a table full of the best food.

decisions.choice: he drew you out: God was luring Job away from distress
alternatives: he would draw you out (an offer still open)
you were being lured away (a warning, as verse 18)
decisions.reason: The verse is difficult, and its words can be divided in more than one way. The most likely sense is that God was drawing Job out of distress to freedom and plenty. The verb usually means to lure or entice, and some read the verse as a warning that Job himself was being lured (the same verb in verse 18), or take it as God's offer still open ("he would draw you out").

decisions.choice: a broad place: freedom and relief
decisions.reason: A wide place where nothing presses in is a picture of rescue, the opposite of the narrow "mouth of distress" (Psalm 18:20; 31:9).

decisions.choice: what was set on your table full of fatness: a table of rich food
decisions.reason: The word for "what was set" (nachat) may come from a verb meaning to set down, or mean quiet and rest ("the quiet of your table"). Fatness means the richest food, a picture of plenty (Psalm 36:9; 63:6).

decisions.choice: God also wanted to lead you
decisions.reason: Readable names God and gives the sense of the verb as an aim (m1).

records.source: וְדִין־רָשָׁ֥ע מָלֵ֑אתָ דִּ֖ין וּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט יִתְמֹֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: And judgment of [the] wicked you are full [of]; judgment and justice take hold.
pieces: But now you are full of the judgment due to the wicked; \q judgment and justice have taken hold of you.

L.17: But you are full of the judgment of the wicked; \q judgment and justice take hold [of you].

R.17: But now you are receiving the punishment that wicked people get; \q judgment has caught up with you.

decisions.choice: full of the judgment of the wicked: under the sentence that falls on the wicked
alternatives: you are taken up with the cause of the wicked
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that Job is full of (receiving) the judgment that falls on the wicked, or that he is full of the wicked's way of pleading, arguing like a wicked man (compare 34:36). The second half, "judgment and justice take hold", fits the first.

decisions.choice: judgment and justice take hold: the verdict seizes Job
decisions.reason: The two words (din and mishpat) together mean legal judgment. The verb means to grasp or hold fast.

decisions.choice: [of you]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object the Hebrew leaves unsaid.

records.source: כִּֽי־חֵ֭מָה פֶּן־יְסִֽיתְךָ֣ בְסָ֑פֶק וְרָב־כֹּ֝֗פֶר אַל־יַטֶּֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: For wrath, lest it entice you into mockery, and [the] greatness of [the] ransom, let it not turn you aside.
pieces: Beware that anger does not lure you into scoffing, \q and do not let a great ransom turn you aside.

L.18: For [beware] lest wrath entice you into scoffing, \q and do not let the greatness of the ransom turn you aside.

R.18: Be careful that anger does not lead you to mock. \q And do not think that a big payment can buy your way out.

decisions.choice: wrath ... entice you: a warning against anger
alternatives: beware of (God's) wrath, lest it strike you
lest it entice you through plenty
decisions.reason: The line is short and compressed: "for wrath, lest it entice you". The wrath may be Job's own anger, which could lead him to scoff at God, or God's wrath, which Job should beware. The word for "mockery" (sefeq) may instead mean plenty, as in the next verse's wealth.

decisions.choice: the greatness of the ransom: a large payment that seems to buy release
alternatives: the heavy price of your suffering
decisions.reason: A ransom (kofer) is a payment for someone's release or life. Elihu warns Job not to think that anything, such as his wealth (verse 19), can buy his way out. In 33:24 Elihu spoke of God finding a ransom; here the ransom may also be the price Job pays in suffering.

decisions.choice: [beware]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the warning word English needs for the clipped Hebrew (m1).

decisions.choice: do not think that a big payment can buy your way out
alternatives: do not let the greatness of the ransom turn you aside
decisions.reason: Readable says what a ransom is and what the warning means (m2).

records.source: הֲיַעֲרֹ֣ךְ שׁ֭וּעֲךָלֹ֣א בְצָ֑ר וְ֝כֹ֗ל מַאֲמַצֵּי־כֹֽחַ׃
records.gloss: Will it set in order your wealth not in distress, and all [the] efforts of strength?
pieces: Can your riches keep you out of distress, \q or all your mighty efforts?

L.19: Will your wealth keep [you] from distress, \q or all the efforts of [your] strength?

R.19: Can your riches keep you out of trouble? \q Can all your strength do it?

decisions.choice: your wealth
decisions.reason: The word (shua') is read as "wealth", as in 34:19, continuing the warning about a ransom (verse 18). The same letters can be a cry for help (30:24): "Will your cry for help avail, without distress?"

decisions.choice: set in order: be enough, avail
decisions.reason: The verb means to arrange or set in order, and from that to match or be equal to (28:17). Here: can wealth be enough to keep Job out of distress?

decisions.choice: [you]; [your]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words the clipped Hebrew leaves unsaid.

records.source: אַל־תִּשְׁאַ֥ף הַלָּ֑יְלָה לַעֲל֖וֹת עַמִּ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: Do not long for the night, for going up of peoples in their place.
pieces: Do not long for the night, \q when peoples are taken away from where they are.

L.20: Do not long for the night, \q when peoples go up from their place.

R.20: Do not wish for the night to come, \q the time when whole nations are carried away.

decisions.choice: the night: the darkness of death or of judgment
alternatives: the night when the wicked act
decisions.reason: The verse is one of the hardest in the speech. The night is probably the night of death, which Job longed for (3:3-10), or the night when nations are suddenly swept away in judgment (34:20, 25). Some think of the night when the wicked do their work (24:14-17).

decisions.choice: peoples go up from their place: they vanish, are removed
decisions.reason: To "go up" here means to be taken away or to vanish, as smoke rises or a sheaf is carried up (5:26). Peoples are swept from where they stood.

decisions.choice: are taken away
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of "go up" here (m2).

records.source: הִ֭שָּׁמֶר אַל־תֵּ֣פֶן אֶל־אָ֑וֶן כִּֽי־עַל־זֶ֝֗ה בָּחַ֥רְתָּ מֵעֹֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Take heed, do not turn to wickedness, for this you have chosen rather than affliction.
pieces: Be careful not to turn to evil, \q for you have preferred it to suffering.

L.21: Take heed; do not turn to wickedness, \q for this you have chosen rather than affliction.

R.21: Be careful not to turn to evil. \q You have been choosing that rather than accepting your suffering.

decisions.choice: this you have chosen rather than affliction
alternatives: for by this you were tested, by affliction
decisions.reason: Elihu charges that Job has preferred wrongdoing, his angry protest against God, to accepting suffering patiently. A slightly different reading of the verb gives "for by this you are tested, by affliction": suffering is God's test.

decisions.choice: wickedness: what is wrong and harmful
decisions.reason: The word ('aven) means evil or iniquity, as in verse 10.

decisions.choice: accepting your suffering
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what choosing against affliction means (m1).

records.source: הֶן־אֵ֭ל יַשְׂגִּ֣יב בְּכֹח֑וֹ מִ֖י כָמֹ֣הוּ מוֹרֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, God is exalted in his power; who like him [is] a teacher?
pieces: God is exalted in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power; \q who is a teacher like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?

L.22: Look, God is exalted in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power; \q who is a teacher like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?

R.22: God is supremely powerful. \q No one teaches the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does.

decisions.choice: is exalted: is high, acts with lofty power
decisions.reason: The verb means to be high or set on high. With verse 26 it frames a call to praise God's greatness.

decisions.choice: teacher: one who instructs
decisions.reason: The word (moreh) means one who teaches or points the way; it comes from the same root as torah, instruction. It suits Elihu's teaching that God instructs people even through suffering (verses 10, 15).

decisions.choice: No one teaches the way he does
alternatives: who is a teacher like him?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

records.source: מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּמִֽי־אָ֝מַ֗ר פָּעַ֥לְתָּ עַוְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: Who has appointed over him his way, and who has said, You have done wrong?
pieces: Who has prescribed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} path for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q or who can say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You have done wrong"?

L.23: Who has appointed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and who has said, "You have done wrong"?

R.23: No one tells God what to do, \q and no one can say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You have done wrong."

decisions.choice: appointed his way: told God what course to take
decisions.reason: The verb (paqad) means to appoint or assign a charge. No one sets God's course for him or calls him to account for it (compare 34:13).

decisions.choice: done wrong: acted unjustly
decisions.reason: The word ('avlah) means injustice or wrongdoing. Elihu rejects what he hears in Job's complaints: that God has wronged him (19:6).

decisions.choice: say to him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "to him", since the words quoted are spoken to God.

decisions.choice: No one tells God what to do
alternatives: Who has appointed his way for him?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into the statements they imply.

records.source: זְ֭כֹר כִּֽי־תַשְׂגִּ֣יא פָעֳל֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר שֹׁרְר֣וּ אֲנָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: Remember that you should magnify his work, which people have sung.
pieces: Remember to praise {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, \q which people have celebrated in song.

L.24: Remember that you should extol {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, \q of which people have sung.

R.24: Remember to praise what God has done; \q people have always sung about it.

decisions.choice: that you should magnify: a call to praise
decisions.reason: The verb form expresses what Job ought to do: instead of accusing God, he should praise his work.

decisions.choice: have sung: celebrated in song
decisions.reason: The verb is read as "sing" (shir). The same letters could come from a verb meaning to look at, which would match "looked" in verse 25.

decisions.choice: what God has done
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says what "his work" means.

records.source: כָּל־אָדָ֥ם חָֽזוּ־ב֑וֹ אֱ֝נ֗וֹשׁ יַבִּ֥יט מֵרָחֽוֹק׃
records.gloss: All humankind have looked on it; mortal man beholds from afar.
pieces: Everyone has seen it; \q people look on it from far away.

L.25: All humankind have looked on it; \q mortals behold [it] from afar.

R.25: Everyone has seen what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done, \q though they see it only from far away.

decisions.choice: from afar: from a distance, seeing only in part
decisions.reason: God's work is plain for all to see, yet human beings look on it from a distance, without grasping it fully (verse 26).

decisions.choice: humankind, mortals: all people
decisions.reason: Both words (adam and enosh) mean human beings in general, not men only; enosh stresses human frailty. Balanced and Readable say "everyone" and "people".

decisions.choice: [it]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object the Hebrew leaves unsaid.

decisions.choice: see it only from far away
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the sense of "from afar" (m1).

records.source: הֶן־אֵ֣ל שַׂ֭גִּיא וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע מִסְפַּ֖ר שָׁנָ֣יו וְלֹא־חֵֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: Look, God [is] great and not we know [him]; the number of his years, and not searching.
pieces: God is great, beyond our knowing; \q the number of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} years cannot be searched out.

L.26: Look, God is great, and we do not know [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]; \q the number of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} years is beyond searching out.

R.26: God is so great that we cannot understand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q His years are too many for anyone to count.

decisions.choice: great: exalted beyond human reach
decisions.reason: The word (saggi') means great or lofty. With verse 22 ("Look, God is exalted") it introduces Elihu's hymn to God's power in rain and storm, which runs through chapter 37.

decisions.choice: the number of his years: God is eternal
decisions.reason: God's years cannot be counted: he has no beginning or end (Psalm 102:28). "No searching" means beyond finding out, as in 5:9 and 9:10.

decisions.choice: [him]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object the Hebrew leaves unsaid.

records.source: כִּ֭י יְגָרַ֣ע נִטְפֵי־מָ֑יִם יָזֹ֖קּוּ מָטָ֣ר לְאֵדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For he draws up drops of water; they refine rain to his mist,
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} draws up the drops of water, \q which distill as rain from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mist,

L.27: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} draws up drops of water; \q they distill as rain from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mist,

R.27: He pulls up drops of water \q and turns {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mist into rain.

decisions.choice: draws up: draws off, takes up
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw off or take away. Here God takes up drops of water, the start of the rain the next lines describe.

decisions.choice: distill as rain from his mist
decisions.reason: The verb (zaqaq) means to refine or filter, as gold is refined (28:1). The mist ('ed) is the moisture of Genesis 2:6. The poet pictures rain as God's work: water drawn up and given back as rain. The sentence runs on into verse 28.

decisions.choice: turns his mist into rain
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words what distilling means here (m2).

records.source: אֲשֶֽׁר־יִזְּל֥וּ שְׁחָקִ֑ים יִ֝רְעֲפ֗וּ עֲלֵ֤י׀אָדָ֬ם רָֽב׃
records.gloss: which pour down [the] clouds; they drip on humankind abundantly.
pieces: which the clouds pour down \q and shower on many people.

L.28: which the clouds pour down; \q they drip on humankind abundantly.

R.28: The clouds pour it down \q in showers on everyone.

decisions.choice: clouds: the thin clouds of the sky
decisions.reason: The word (shechaqim) means the clouds or the skies, often the high, thin clouds (37:18, 21).

decisions.choice: on humankind abundantly: on many people
decisions.reason: The last word (rav) can describe the rain (abundantly) or the people (on many people). Either way, the rain falls generously on all.

decisions.choice: on everyone
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words that the rain reaches all people (m2).

records.source: אַ֣ף אִם־יָ֭בִין מִפְרְשֵׂי־עָ֑ב תְּ֝שֻׁא֗וֹת סֻכָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Also if one understands [the] spreadings of [the] cloud, [the] crashings of his pavilion?
pieces: Can anyone understand how the clouds spread out, \q or the thunder from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} pavilion?

L.29: Indeed, can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, \q the thunderings of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} pavilion?

R.29: Who can understand how the clouds spread across the sky, \q or the thunder that rolls from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tent in the sky?

decisions.choice: if one understands: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The "if" introduces a question with the answer left unsaid: no one understands.

decisions.choice: his pavilion: the dark storm clouds as God's shelter
decisions.reason: The word (sukkah) means a booth or shelter. In Psalm 18:12 God makes dark storm clouds his shelter; here the thunder roars from it.

decisions.choice: his tent in the sky
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the pavilion (m2).

records.source: הֵן־פָּרַ֣שׂ עָלָ֣יו אוֹר֑וֹ וְשָׁרְשֵׁ֖י הַיָּ֣ם כִּסָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, he spreads over him his light, and [the] roots of the sea he covers.
pieces: See how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} scatters {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lightning around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q and covers the depths of the sea.

L.30: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spreads {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light around {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} covers the roots of the sea.

R.30: He scatters lightning all around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} covers the bottom of the sea.

decisions.choice: his light: his lightning
decisions.reason: In this storm poem light often means lightning (36:32; 37:3, 11, 15).

decisions.choice: the roots of the sea: its deepest parts
alternatives: he bares the depths of the sea
decisions.reason: The roots of the sea are its bottom (compare Jonah 2:7, the roots of the mountains). It is not clear whether God covers them with his light, so that it reaches the depths, or covers them in darkness under the storm.

decisions.choice: lightning
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "light" here (m1).

records.source: כִּי־בָ֭ם יָדִ֣ין עַמִּ֑ים יִֽתֶּן־אֹ֥כֶל לְמַכְבִּֽיר׃
records.gloss: For by them he judges peoples; he gives food in abundance.
pieces: For by these {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges the peoples \q and gives food in abundance.

L.31: For by these {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges peoples; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives food in abundance.

R.31: He uses the rain and storms to judge nations \q and to give people plenty of food.

decisions.choice: by these: by the clouds, rain and lightning
decisions.reason: "These" are the works just described. The storm can bring judgment (floods and lightning) or food (rain for crops); 37:13 makes the same point.

decisions.choice: judges: judges or governs
decisions.reason: The verb (din) means to judge, and from that to govern. Some read a verb with similar letters, "nourishes", to match "food" in the next line.

decisions.choice: the rain and storms
decisions.reason: Readable names what "these" refers to (m1).

records.source: עַל־כַּפַּ֥יִם כִּסָּה־א֑וֹר וַיְצַ֖ו עָלֶ֣יהָ בְמַפְגִּֽיעַ׃
records.gloss: Over [the] palms he covers [with] light, and he commands it to [the] one who strikes.
pieces: He fills {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands with lightning \q and commands it to strike the mark.

L.32: He covers [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands with light, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands it to strike the mark.

R.32: He holds lightning in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands \q and orders it to hit its target.

decisions.choice: covers the palms with light: holds lightning in his hands
alternatives: he hides the light with his hands
decisions.reason: The picture is of God holding the lightning in his hands as a weapon (compare Habakkuk 3:4). It may instead mean that God hides the light behind his hands, the clouds.

decisions.choice: to strike the mark: against the target
decisions.reason: The last word (mafgia') means one who strikes or what is struck. God aims the lightning like an arrow at its target.

decisions.choice: [his]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the word English needs for the compressed line, which says only "over palms he covers light".

records.source: יַגִּ֣יד עָלָ֣יו רֵע֑וֹ מִ֝קְנֶ֗ה אַ֣ף עַל־עוֹלֶֽה׃
records.gloss: It declares concerning him his thunder; [the] cattle also concerning [what] rises.
pieces: His thunder announces {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming; \q even the cattle sense the storm rising.

L.33: His thunder declares concerning {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q the cattle also, concerning what rises.

R.33: The thunder tells that God is coming; \q even the cattle know that a storm is on the way.

decisions.choice: the thunder announces God; even cattle sense the rising storm
alternatives: his thunder tells of him, of his zealous anger against wrongdoing
decisions.reason: This is one of the most uncertain verses in Job. The word read here as "his thunder" (re'a) can also mean "his friend". The word for "cattle" (miqneh), with different vowels, can be read as "jealous anger", giving "he is zealous with anger against wrongdoing" (reading the last word as "injustice" instead of "what rises"). The reading kept here follows the Hebrew letters as they stand.

decisions.choice: what rises: the storm coming up
decisions.reason: The last word means "one who goes up": most likely the storm rising in the sky, which animals sense before it comes.

decisions.choice: announces his coming
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the most likely sense of "declares concerning him" (m1).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one the thunder announces.
